## 固定收益開篇論點

6月12日，美國公債未能延續前一收盤日由油價帶動的存續期間漲勢。美伊協議取得進展，推動原油下跌，美國公債早盤一度跟隨歐洲債市上漲，但漲幅其後消退，終場小幅收低。2年期殖利率收於4.09%，上升4個基點；10年期收於4.48%，上升3個基點。前端表現落後、殖利率曲線小幅趨平，顯示市場重新計入政策溢價，而非反映新一波長端財政衝擊。

這波逆轉使6月11日僅暫時延後的問題重新浮現。能源價格下跌，降低再度出現大規模第一輪通膨衝擊的機率，卻未消除已逐步傳導至生產者價格、家庭預期及海外央行政策反應的壓力。市場再度大幅提高聯準會年底前升息的權重。消費者信心改善、通膨預期下降，讓官員有條件繼續觀望，但兩項指標的絕對水準仍不足以支持政策迅速轉向寬鬆。

全球債市也強化了這項限制。和平消息帶動歐洲前端債券大幅上漲，但歐洲央行官員強調，即使衝突結束，較廣泛的價格壓力仍可能迫使央行進一步緊縮。英國4月經濟萎縮，家庭通膨預期卻大幅上升。兩股力量相互牽制，使已開發市場債券仍須以偏高殖利率才能出清：經濟活動轉弱在邊際上支撐債市，能源成本傳導與政策信譽考量則限制殖利率的下行空間。

風險資產將本交易日解讀為地緣情勢降溫，而非經濟步入衰退。股市上漲、波動率下降、美元走軟，信用基金價格大致持穩，削弱前一收盤日支撐美國公債的防禦性買盤。信用市場融資管道仍然暢通，但選擇性鮮明：日圓計價銀行債需求強勁，資金也持續轉向優先順位較高的CLO曝險。因此，市場主軸已由全面反映地緣政治利多，轉為政策因素主導的盤整。油價下跌改善尾端風險分布，但風險偏好具韌性、聯準會提前升息的風險，以及海外通膨限制，使美國殖利率未能連續第2天下滑。

## 美國公債利率、Fed定價、實質殖利率與殖利率曲線結構

美國公債跌勢集中於政策敏感端。2年期殖利率上升4個基點至4.09%，5年期上升3個基點至4.21%，10年期上升3個基點至4.48%，30年期上升2個基點至4.97%。30年期殖利率仍低於前一日債市上漲時重新跌破的5%門檻，且升幅小於其他年期，不支持財政或存續期間因素獨立引發衝擊的解讀。相較之下，本交易日主要收復了部分先前消退的政策溢價；地緣政治情勢改善時，市場曾將聯準會下一步行動推遲，使這部分溢價下降。

殖利率曲線小幅趨平。2s10s利差收窄1個基點至39個基點，2s30s利差收窄2個基點至88個基點。曲線曲率仍然有序：2s5s10s蝶式利差下降1個基點至負15個基點，2s10s30s蝶式利差則持平於負10個基點。全週而言，2年期與5年期殖利率仍各下降8個基點，10年期下降7個基點，30年期下降4個基點。因此，6月12日僅回吐部分單週漲幅，單日調整集中於前端，並非市場全面排斥存續期間部位。

實質殖利率與通膨補償同步推升名目殖利率。10年期實質殖利率上升1個基點至2.17%，10年期損益兩平通膨率上升2個基點至2.31%。5年期實質殖利率上升4個基點至1.82%，7年期上升2個基點至1.98%，20年期與30年期則持平至上升1個基點。前端至中段實質殖利率調整較大，符合市場重新反映政策約束的走勢；損益兩平通膨率小幅上升，則顯示現貨原油下跌尚未完全消除市場對價格滯後傳導的疑慮。

盤中走勢使收盤結果格外值得注意。市場看好荷姆茲海峽重新開放，Brent原油在歐洲交易時段跌破每桶$86，英國與德國2年期公債的漲幅也遠大於美國公債。美國2年期殖利率在週四尾盤大幅下滑後，週五早盤一度續跌。然而，即使油價再度下跌，美國公債殖利率終場仍然走高，顯示地緣情勢降溫已不足以單獨主導市場。市場焦點由地緣政治尾端風險消退，轉向先前能源衝擊已有多少反映在通膨及貨幣政策之中。

短期利率定價提供了最明確的答案。債券交易員認為聯準會年底前升息的機率約為75%，並已完全反映2027年3月前升息1次。6月11日一度後移的提前升息風險因而重新浮現。經濟學家的看法仍較溫和：一項涵蓋35人的調查顯示，預測中位數為2027年6月首次降息，同年12月再降息1次，使目標利率區間降至3%-3.25%。兩種觀點都排除近期寬鬆，但在經濟活動具韌性、戰爭推升通膨的情境下，市場對政策重新收緊賦予更高權重。

密西根大學初步調查形成實質反向力量，但仍不足以釐清政策前景。消費者信心指數由44.8升至48.9，其中現況指數為48.4，預期指數為49.3。1年期通膨預期由4.8%降至4.6%，長期通膨預期則由3.9%降至3.4%。通膨預期下降，降低政策立即回應的迫切性；然而，通膨預期仍處高檔，加上消費者信心轉強，顯示家庭需求與價格預期仍有韌性，前端市場無法將這項改善視為持久的通膨降溫訊號。

勞動成本水準構成另一項限制。3月民間受僱者平均每小時薪酬為$49.32，其中工資為$33.72、福利為$15.60；私人產業平均每小時薪酬為$46.60。去年12月的相應水準分別為$48.78及$46.15。這些數字是薪酬水準，並非就業成本指數的成長率，但薪酬上升仍使企業利潤率及服務價格黏著度受到關注。這項數據並未否定密西根大學調查所顯示的通膨預期下降，而是說明政策制定者為何仍須確認價格壓力緩解已擴及能源以外領域。

極短期融資市場維持有序。以附息債等值殖利率計算，4週期與6週期國庫券分別收於3.66%及3.67%，均下降1個基點。8週期、13週期、17週期及26週期殖利率分別持平於3.69%、3.71%、3.76%及3.80%，52週期殖利率則上升1個基點至3.86%。最短天期的現金市場未隨附息債走弱。相反地，殖利率向1年期逐步上斜，反映未來可能出現的政策調整，也區隔了當前流動性充裕與聯準會日後可能必須提高目標利率的風險。

## 信用、融資與初級市場承接

信用市場未受美國公債溫和賣壓明顯影響。LQD下跌0.0642%，符合其政府債券存續期間曝險；HYG持平，JNK則上漲0.0208%。高收益債基金未同步下跌，與股市上漲、波動率下降的走勢一致，顯示6月12日並未出現資金全面撤離企業風險的情況。美國公債殖利率上升因而較適合從政策定價與避險需求減弱解讀，而非企業融資環境惡化。

Lloyds Banking Group的交易顯示，優質借款人仍能取得跨幣別融資。該行發行¥750億武士債，為2年來首次進入日本國內債券市場。截至6月12日，本會計年度武士債發行量已達¥5,030億，創2015年以來同期新高。日本投資人偏好相對較短的年期，以及較日本國內替代標的更寬的利差；即使計入換匯成本，部分海外發行人以日圓融資仍具成本效益。

這筆交易以明顯的新券讓利完成承接，並非投資人不分標的一概追捧。Lloyds的6年期券可於第5年後贖回，定價為交換利率加78個基點。評等較Lloyds高1級的Sumitomo Mitsui Banking，4月發行一檔2031年到期債券，定價為交換利率加28個基點。兩者的利差差距補償發行人信用與債券結構的差異，但未妨礙Lloyds完成發行。只要相對利差、到期年限及換匯後融資成本相互配合，即使日本利率上升，外國發行人仍可進入當地市場融資。

兩筆潛在交易顯示，市場選擇性不只存在於高評級跨幣別融資。銀行為Triton收購德國齒輪製造商Flender籌組約€17億槓桿貸款，預計6月底開始推介。新資金交易供給稀少，有利借款人壓低定價，但一般聯貸程序仍須驗證機構需求。烏克蘭鋼鐵商Metinvest則在先前再融資失敗、改以內部現金償還4月到期的$4.28億債券後，評估重返市場；其2029年10月到期債券4月初殖利率一度超過12.5%。前者是受惠於供給稀缺的私募股權收購融資，後者則是受戰爭影響的發行人；能以現金還債，尚不足以證明已有持續進入市場的能力。

槓桿信用市場內部的需求更加分化。年初以來，美國CLO ETF淨流入超過$90億，高於2025年同期的近$70億；同一期間，投資人則持續撤出上市商業發展公司。基準利率偏高，有利浮動利率貸款收益，但借款成本長期居高，也會削弱標的企業的財務體質。優先順位CLO分券透過次順位保障，先由次順位部位吸收損失，再影響最高順位投資人。隨著市場更加關注私人信用違約風險，受償結構與流動性也成為投資決策的關鍵。

基金流向與武士債發行共同顯示，金融中介功能正常，但資金配置標準相當明確。可公開交易的優先順位貸款結構吸引資金，高評等外國銀行也藉由支付明顯利差溢價進入日本市場。這兩項發展均不代表美國企業借款人的現券利差全面轉鬆，而是顯示，只要投資人能確認受償順位較高、流動性透明，或新券讓利具相對價值，市場仍願意提供資金。這種選擇性承接能力，使信用市場在政策敏感端的美國公債殖利率上升時仍維持平穩。

## 全球存續期間、央行與財政傳導

歐洲前端債券起初對油價回落的反應遠比美國公債強烈。和平前景降低近期升息押注，英國2年期公債殖利率下降14個基點至4.20%，德國2年期公債殖利率也下跌近10個基點至2.58%。此前歐洲央行才剛進行2023年以來首次升息，英國成長數據則偏弱，因此歐洲殖利率曲線有較多政策溢價可供回吐。美國殖利率其後逆轉，顯示歐洲債市的高敏感度並不代表已開發市場一致認定通膨將持續降溫。

歐洲央行的政策溝通，限制了這波債市漲勢的政策意義。央行已將存款利率上調25個基點至2.25%，Peter Kazimir並表示，若價格壓力持續擴散，仍須採取進一步行動。歐元區5月通膨率達3.2%，修訂後的展望則顯示，核心通膨至少到2028年仍將高於目標。市場仍反映2026年再升息1次，並認為2027年上半年另一次升息的機率為70%。和平協議可能迅速壓低能源價格，但產能受損及供應鏈傳導效應，仍可能使整體通膨維持高檔。

歐洲官員的立場並非一致偏鷹。部分官員認為，在取得更多數據前，最近一次升息已經足夠；經濟活動低迷也限制政策進一步緊縮的幅度。這項分歧同樣影響美國公債。歐洲央行若在近期連續升息，將提高其他高評等資產的前端報酬；但經濟成長若最終反轉，也會增加德國公債及美國公債需求。6月12日歐洲債市的漲勢較多反映後者，美國收盤則保留較多前者的影響。

英國數據進一步凸顯相同矛盾。4月GDP較前月萎縮0.1%，扭轉3月成長0.3%的表現，並創2025年8月以來首次下降。服務業下滑0.2%，生產持平，營建業則成長0.1%。截至4月的3個月仍成長0.7%，略優於前一個3個月期間。英國公債投資人面對的是單月經濟轉弱，但成長動能尚未明顯崩落。油價回落因此能夠支撐前端債券，中期利率路徑則仍取決於通膨。

家庭通膨預期仍使英格蘭銀行受到約束。1年期通膨預期中位數由2月的3.2%升至4.0%，5年期通膨預期則由3.7%升至3.9%。預期未來1年利率上升的受訪者占53%，高於先前的30%。這些數據顯示，僅憑單月產出轉弱，尚不足以重啟寬鬆循環，也解釋了油價下跌為何能帶動英國公債單日大漲，卻無法排除政策重新收緊的風險。

德國央行的預測量化財政支出如何支撐成長，卻未消除歐洲央行的通膨問題。央行預計德國GDP在2026年、2027年及2028年分別成長0.5%、0.8%與1.4%，公共支出將抵銷部分戰爭衝擊；通膨則預計今年達2.9%、2027年為2.7%，直到2028年才降至1.9%。財政支援提高成長底部，也可能延緩通膨下降，使德國前端政策風險有別於近期疲弱的工業數據。

波蘭則朝相反方向發展。貨幣政策委員Ireneusz Dabrowski表示，5月通膨意外降至3.1%後，10人委員會幾乎全體對再次升息的擔憂均已降低，使3.75%政策利率在2026年出現降息空間。這是條件式訊號而非正式決策，但讓新興市場分歧更加明確：決定央行是否保留緊縮傾向的，是各國自身通膨證據，而不只是共同油價衝擊。

週末澳洲資訊把這項分歧延伸至已開發市場。經濟成長與就業轉弱、通膨動能略降後，經濟學家預期澳洲央行在2026年連續升息3次後，將利率維持在4.35%。市場對12月前再升息的定價由完全反映降至約60%。長債投資人押注10年期殖利率朝4.5%下降，短端投資人預期最終將降息，防禦型資金則偏好抗通膨債券。各方均認為緊縮循環接近尾聲，但對成長轉弱或通膨黏著何者主導後續走勢，仍有明顯分歧。

日本長端債市則面臨投資人基礎轉變。4月外國投資人賣出的超長期日本公債多於買進，為2024年以來首次。即使殖利率升至數十年高點，市場對通膨、財政供給，以及日本央行被認為落後情勢的疑慮，仍壓過收益率的吸引力。不過，日本國內需求並未消失。Iyogin自4月起小額買進超長期日本公債，為10年來首次投資JGB，相關部位納入其¥1.7兆證券投資組合。外國資產管理機構撤退、區域銀行選擇性重返，意味債券須以更高且更不穩定的殖利率出清，而非需求單向消失。

週末匯率部位使日本央行決策面臨不對稱風險。日圓空頭升至9年來最高，美日利差持續支撐carry交易；但市場已大致反映日本央行升息及匯率干預。2024年的前例仍值得注意：央行意外升息並宣布加速縮減購債後，日圓快速反彈，迫使槓桿部位平倉，衝擊全球匯率與股市。因此，如果日本央行超出預期，擁擠空頭可能放大日圓升值與全球去槓桿；若升息完全符合預期且指引審慎，carry交易則可能延續。

這些海外發展會透過相對殖利率與避險成本影響美國公債。歐洲貨幣政策可使當地前端資產維持報酬競爭力；超長期JGB波動加劇，則可能降低日本機構增持海外長存續期間資產的意願，即使美國名目殖利率仍高。英國成長疲弱，以及日本國內投資人選擇性買進JGB，則提供部分抵銷。各市場之間的資金競爭，有助解釋原油大跌為何能在盤中推升歐洲債市，卻無法讓美國公債漲勢延續至紐約收盤。

## 新興市場主權債、美元流動性與債務管理風險

印尼顯示，即使全球環境改善，本地流動性仍可能受損。兩檔債券基金因政府公債在資產賣壓與印尼盾波動後難以出售，而延後辦理贖回。規模據報為印尼盾5.7兆的KIM Fixed Income Fund Plus，截至週四當週下跌1.5%；印尼盾6,914億的伊斯蘭基金則下跌0.7%。印尼央行減少買進政府公債，並在例會外升息，目的是容許殖利率上升以支撐匯率，卻也收緊債券市場流動性。延長贖回週期使問題由價格波動轉為基金負債管理，也顯示匯率防衛策略可能削弱國內買方基礎。

新興市場債券的整體環境略有改善。EMB上漲0.0935%，美元指數走軟、原油下跌，既減輕美元融資壓力，也降低石油進口國未來的能源支出。EMB漲幅遠小於股市與波動率的變化，顯示個別國家的財政與政策風險仍限制利多。孟加拉則呈現更直接的能源供應如何限制投資。Cumilla經濟區內包括鋼鐵、玻璃及鋁業在內、接近$7.5億的工業投資，因天然氣供應未能到位而停滯；平均零售電價同時上調17%，5月通膨升至16個月高點。實體能源不足一方面降低未來生產能力，另一方面提高家庭與企業成本。這與暫時性的市場價格衝擊不同：即使全球燃料價格下降，供應無法取得仍可能削弱成長、稅收與外部競爭力。

印度最能反映這項矛盾：通膨放緩有利債市，財政赤字可能擴大則帶來反向壓力。

據報導，若全球環境有此需要，印度當局願意容許財政赤字由GDP的4.3%目標擴大至最高4.8%。印度超過80%的原油仰賴進口，燃料及肥料補貼增加已對預算構成壓力。印度10年期公債殖利率盤中一度觸及6.91%，其後回落至6.88%。一項估計認為，政府可能額外發行3,500億盧比國庫券。這使債務管理成為赤字擴大的具體後果，而不僅是帳面調整。

最新通膨數據提供部分抵銷。5月CPI年增3.93%，低於市場共識的4.02%，也略低於印度央行4%的目標。數據公布後，10年期公債維持漲勢，殖利率報6.89%。不過，食品通膨由4.20%加速至4.78%，印度央行也已將本會計年度通膨預測由4.6%上調至5.1%。整體通膨低於預期使主權債受益，但食品價格、匯率與補貼曝險，仍使財政信譽及舉債因應成為影響殖利率曲線的核心因素。

巴西則出現反方向的通膨意外。5月消費者物價月增0.58%，高於0.53%的預估中位數；年增率達4.72%，超過通膨目標區間4.5%的上限。食品及飲料價格上漲1.33%，基礎價格壓力也擴及受戰爭直接影響較小的項目。Selic政策利率已達14.5%，這份數據進一步壓縮降息空間。巴西當地資產雖因此維持高利差收益，代價卻是國內融資條件更加緊縮。

新興市場的政策走向持續分化。印尼先前透過例會以外的升息穩定匯率並扭轉市場賣壓；通膨放緩則引發波蘭與匈牙利是否轉向寬鬆的討論。羅馬尼亞通膨升至3年高點，支持央行維持利率不變，捷克官員則仍保留升息可能。相較於由可信政策框架支撐的高利差市場，亞洲石油進口國更容易受到油價再次上漲的衝擊。美元略為走軟，雖可緩解各國共同面臨的外部限制，卻無法消除通膨走勢及央行信譽的差異。

委內瑞拉週末出現顧問競標，為潛在債務重整帶來具體費用與治理變化。Lazard提議以$2,500萬承辦估計介於$1,500億至$2,000億的重整，遠低於Centerview先前討論的至少$1.5億安排；後者包括重整債務0.1%、未設上限的成功報酬，以及每月$75萬顧問費。顧問是否更換及債權人條件均未確定，但競爭性報價顯示程序成本可以協商；在核對債券、貸款、仲裁與其他債權前，顧問任命的治理方式就可能影響可分配價值。

次主權實體進入資本市場的能力，仍不及中央政府的政策彈性。中央政府移轉款削減約印尼盾15兆，約占原始預算16%後，雅加達持續研議發行印尼首檔市政債券。這項債券計畫及擬成立的主權財富基金，仍待財政部核准。計畫可望使基礎建設融資來源更多元，但其高度依賴監管核准，加上中央移轉款減少，顯示地方政府自行創造信用不能等同於主權國家進入市場融資。整體而言，油價下跌改善新興市場當日環境，但再融資結構、外匯存底運用，以及財政調整的可信度，仍決定各國能實際取得多少助益。

## 跨資產

股市走勢進一步支持美國公債因避險買盤消退而下跌，而非市場擔憂經濟成長轉弱。S&P 500上漲0.5026%，Nasdaq 100上漲0.6445%，半導體指數上漲1.5187%。科技股領漲，反映市場對名目經濟活動及AI資本支出延續仍有信心。即使能源價格下跌改善通膨展望，這種環境仍會推升殖利率曲線前端及中段的實質折現率。

波動率與美元也反映風險偏好升溫。VIX下跌9.0535%至17.68，美元指數下滑0.1102%至99.75。波動率下降，削弱市場對長存續期間防禦性資產的需求；美元走軟，則改善新興市場借款人的外部融資環境。整體走勢不像全球美元短缺或全面去槓桿，也有助解釋高收益債基金價格為何持穩。

能源市場形成當日最重要的矛盾。談判提高荷姆茲海峽重新開放的希望，WTI下跌3.2265%至每桶$84.88，Brent原油下跌3.3746%至每桶$87.33。然而，美國公債損益兩平通膨率與名目殖利率終場均走高。這項背離顯示，市場已在6月11日反映大部分即時的地緣情勢降溫利多，焦點轉向通膨的滯後效應、經濟活動韌性及聯準會的政策反應。原油下跌改善各種可能結果的分布，卻未決定利率的收盤方向。

黃金並未完全呼應偏向樂觀的市場解讀。即使股市上漲、油價下跌、波動率下降，黃金期貨仍上漲3.0487%至每盎司$4,215。儘管市場看好談判進展，通膨與地緣政治避險需求仍然存在，跨資產走勢因而不是單純解除戰爭風險部位。黃金與損益兩平通膨率同步上升，也提醒市場：協議尚未恢復受損產能，落實過程仍有不確定性。

SpaceX創紀錄的首次公開發行，凸顯市場風險偏好的強度。股票發行價為$135，掛牌後以$150開盤，盤中最高升至$163；這筆募資規模達$750億，股價首日收高19%。市場消化如此龐大的發行量之際，主要股價指數仍然上漲，反映成長型資產需求深厚。這也強化實質利率維持高檔的資本密集支出機制：即使地緣政治情勢改善，降低當前通膨溢價，AI與基礎建設投資仍持續爭取市場儲蓄資金。

## 前瞻市場意義

6月15日至17日公布的美國經濟活動、貿易價格及消費數據，最終將銜接6月17日美東時間14:00的聯邦公開市場委員會決策，以及主席Kevin Warsh於14:30舉行的首次會後記者會。市場首先要觀察，在進口價格降溫之際，工業生產與零售銷售是否仍具韌性；其後則須檢視點陣圖及政策聲明是否保留明確的緊縮傾向。需求穩健、貿易價格廣泛上漲，或利率預測指向升息，都將推升2年期及5年期殖利率，確認6月12日重新建立的政策溢價。若經濟活動轉弱、價格上漲廣度收斂，且政策指引轉為中性，則會削弱提前升息的解讀，並重新開啟6月11日出現的實質殖利率下行空間。

6月12日資料截止後，巴基斯坦總理表示，美國與伊朗已同意立即停止軍事行動、解除美國海軍封鎖，並於6月19日在瑞士正式簽署協議。後續執行情況將決定週五油價下跌能否轉化為持久的通膨降溫動力。市場須觀察荷姆茲海峽能否持續通航、敵對行動是否停止、原油價格是否續跌，以及家庭與市場通膨預期是否回落。若協議順利落實，將確認能源價格下降最終可帶動損益兩平通膨率及全球前端殖利率走低；若簽署前進度受阻、封鎖風險再現，或核心價格壓力持續，則會削弱這項判斷，並可能在現貨油價下跌之際重新推升通膨溢價。

6月15日至18日的美國公債標售日程，將檢驗政策不確定性升高之際，市場資產負債表能否有序承接供給。6月15日首先標售$890億13週期國庫券及$770億26週期國庫券；6月16日接著標售$650億6週期國庫券，並增額發行$130億20年期公債；6月18日再增額發行$240億5年期抗通膨債券。6月19日固定收益市場休市，也將縮短市場反應時間。觀察重點包括國庫券需求、融資利率、20年期得標利率相對發行前交易水準的差距、投標者配售結構，以及實質殖利率需求。若終端投資人承接強勁、現金利率穩定，近期供給疑慮便可望消退，並確認本輪賣壓由總體因素主導。若交易商承接比例偏高、出現標售尾差或融資壓力，財政供給就會重新成為期限溢價的獨立上行因素。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

June 12 was a failed extension of the previous close’s oil-led duration rally. Treasuries initially joined the renewed bid in European bonds as progress toward a US-Iran agreement pushed crude lower, but the US move faded and the curve ended modestly cheaper. The 2-year yield finished at 4.09%, 4 basis points higher, and the 10-year at 4.48%, 3 basis points higher. Front-end underperformance and a slight flattening showed that the market was rebuilding policy premium, not imposing a fresh long-end fiscal shock.

The reversal reopened an issue that June 11 had only deferred. Falling energy prices reduced the probability of another large first-round inflation impulse, yet they did not erase pressure already moving through producer prices, household expectations and foreign central-bank reaction functions. Market pricing again assigned substantial weight to a Federal Reserve increase before year-end. A better consumer-sentiment reading and lower inflation expectations gave officials room to wait, but their absolute levels remained inconsistent with a quick return to an easing narrative.

Global duration reinforced that constraint. European front ends rallied more strongly on the peace headlines, although ECB officials emphasized that broader price pressure could require additional tightening even if the conflict ended. UK growth contracted in April, but household inflation expectations rose sharply. Those opposing signals preserved a high clearing rate for developed-market duration: weaker activity supported bonds at the margin, whereas energy pass-through and policy credibility limited how far yields could fall.

Risk assets treated the session as de-escalation rather than recession. Equities advanced, volatility fell, the dollar softened and credit fund prices were broadly stable. That configuration reduced the defensive demand that had helped Treasuries on the previous close. Credit access also remained selective rather than impaired, with strong demand for a yen-denominated bank issue and continuing migration toward senior CLO exposure. The governing thesis therefore changed from broad geopolitical relief to a policy-led consolidation: cheaper oil improved the tail-risk distribution, but resilient risk appetite, earlier Fed-hike risk and foreign inflation constraints prevented a 2nd day of lower US yields.

## UST Rates, Fed Pricing, Real Yields, And Curve Structure

Treasury losses were concentrated in the policy-sensitive end. The 2-year yield rose 4 basis points to 4.09%, the 5-year added 3 to 4.21%, the 10-year increased 3 to 4.48%, and the 30-year gained 2 to 4.97%. The long bond remained below the 5% threshold regained during the prior day’s rally, and the smaller move at 30 years argues against an independent fiscal or duration shock. The session instead restored part of the premium removed when geopolitical relief had pushed expectations for the next Fed move farther out.

The curve flattened modestly. The 2s10s slope narrowed 1 basis point to 39, and 2s30s narrowed 2 to 88. Curvature remained orderly: the 2s5s10s butterfly fell 1 basis point to -15, whereas the 2s10s30s butterfly was unchanged at -10. Over the week, yields were still lower by 8 basis points at 2 and 5 years, seven at 10 years and four at 30 years. June 12 therefore retraced only part of the week’s rally, with the daily adjustment centered on the front end rather than a wholesale rejection of duration.

Real rates and inflation compensation both contributed to the nominal move. The 10-year real yield rose 1 basis point to 2.17%, and the 10-year breakeven increased 2 to 2.31%. 5-year real yields climbed 4 basis points to 1.82%, 7-year real yields rose 2 to 1.98%, and the 20- and 30-year sectors were unchanged to 1 basis point higher. The larger front-belly real-yield adjustment fits renewed policy restraint, whereas the small breakeven increase showed that lower spot crude had not fully displaced concern about lagged price transmission.

Intraday sequencing made the close especially informative. Optimism over reopening the Strait of Hormuz drove Brent below $86 during European trading and produced a much larger rally in UK and German 2-year debt than in Treasuries. US 2-year yields were briefly lower early in the day after a sharp decline late Thursday. Finishing higher despite another drop in oil meant that the de-escalation impulse had become insufficient on its own. The market moved from pricing the removal of a geopolitical tail toward asking how much of the earlier energy shock was already embedded in inflation and policy.

Short-rate expectations supplied the clearest answer. Bond traders assigned roughly a 75% chance to a Fed increase by year-end and fully priced a move by March 2027. That reopened the earlier-hike risk that had shifted outward on June 11. Economists remained less aggressive: the median forecast in a 35-person survey placed the 1st cut in June 2027 and another by that December, taking the target range to 3%-3.25%. Both views rejected near-term easing, but the market attached more weight to renewed restraint under resilient activity and war-driven inflation.

The preliminary University of Michigan survey offered a real counterforce without settling the policy question. Sentiment rose to 48.9 from 44.8, with current conditions at 48.4 and expectations at 49.3. 1-year inflation expectations eased to 4.6% from 4.8%, and the long-run measure fell to 3.4% from 3.9%. The decline in expected inflation reduced the urgency of an immediate response. Its still-elevated level, combined with firmer confidence, left household demand and price psychology too strong for the front end to treat the improvement as a durable disinflation signal.

Labor-cost levels added a secondary constraint. Civilian employer compensation averaged $49.32 per hour in March, including $33.72 in wages and $15.60 in benefits; private-industry compensation averaged $46.60. The corresponding December levels were $48.78 and $46.15. These are compensation levels rather than an Employment Cost Index growth rate, but the increase preserves concern about business margins and service-price persistence. The release did not contradict the softer Michigan expectations; it showed why policymakers still need confirmation that price relief extends beyond energy.

Very short funding remained orderly. Coupon-equivalent bill yields ended at 3.66% for 4 weeks and 3.67% for 6 weeks, both 1 basis point lower. 8-, 13-, 17- and 26-week yields were unchanged at 3.69%, 3.71%, 3.76% and 3.80%, while the 52-week yield rose 1 basis point to 3.86%. Cash conditions at the shortest tenors did not participate in the coupon selloff. The upward slope toward 1 year instead carried the prospective policy adjustment, separating ample immediate liquidity from the risk that the Fed may need to raise its target later.

## Credit, Funding, And Primary-Market Absorption

Credit was stable through the mild Treasury selloff. LQD slipped 0.0642%, a move consistent with its government-duration exposure, while HYG was unchanged and JNK gained 0.0208%. The absence of a parallel decline in the high-yield funds fits the equity advance and lower volatility: June 12 did not produce a broad withdrawal from corporate risk. It also means the rise in Treasury yields is better read through policy and haven demand than through a deterioration in corporate financing conditions.

Lloyds Banking Group demonstrated that cross-currency funding remained available to strong borrowers. The bank sold ¥75 billion of Samurai bonds, its 1st domestic Japanese offering in 2 years. Fiscal-year issuance in the market had reached ¥503 billion by June 12, the strongest comparable total since 2015. Japanese investors were drawn to relatively short maturities and spreads wider than domestic alternatives, and yen funding remained economical for some overseas issuers even after currency-swap costs.

The pricing showed absorption with a meaningful concession rather than indiscriminate demand. Lloyds’ 6-year tranche, callable after 5 years, paid 78 basis points over swaps. A Sumitomo Mitsui Banking note due in 2031 had priced at 28 basis points in April, with the Japanese bank rated one notch above Lloyds by S&P. The gap compensated investors for issuer and structure differences, yet it did not prevent execution. A rising-rate Japan can therefore support foreign issuance when relative spread, maturity and swapped funding cost align.

Two prospective transactions showed how that selectivity extended beyond high-grade cross-currency funding. Banks arranged about €1.7 billion of leveraged loans for Triton's acquisition of German gearbox maker Flender, with marketing scheduled for late June. Scarce new-money supply was helping borrowers compress pricing, but general syndication still had to test institutional demand. Ukrainian steel producer Metinvest separately explored a return after using internal cash to redeem a $428 million April maturity when earlier refinancing plans failed; its October 2029 bond had yielded more than 12.5% in early April. The cases separated a sponsor-backed acquisition benefiting from supply scarcity from a conflict-exposed issuer whose ability to pay from cash did not yet establish durable market access.

Demand inside leveraged credit was more segmented. Inflows into US CLO exchange-traded funds exceeded $9 billion during the year, up from nearly $7 billion over the same period of 2025, as investors pulled money from publicly traded business-development companies. Elevated base rates support the income on floating-rate loans, but prolonged borrowing costs also weaken the underlying companies. Senior CLO tranches use subordination to absorb losses before top-ranked investors are affected, making structure and liquidity decisive as concern about private-credit defaults increases.

Together, the fund flows and Samurai sale describe functioning but discriminating intermediation. Publicly tradeable senior loan structures attracted money, and a highly rated foreign bank accessed Japan by paying a visible spread premium. Neither development implies uniformly easier cash spreads for US borrowers. They show that capital was available where investors could identify a strong payment priority, transparent liquidity or an attractive relative-value concession. That selective capacity helped keep credit calm even as policy-sensitive Treasury yields rose.

## Global Duration, Central Banks, And Fiscal Transmission

European front ends initially expressed the oil relief more forcefully than Treasuries. UK 2-year yields fell 14 basis points to 4.20%, and German 2-year yields dropped nearly 10 basis points to 2.58% as peace prospects reduced near-term hike bets. The move followed the ECB’s 1st increase since 2023 and weak UK growth, giving European curves more policy premium to unwind. US yields’ later reversal showed that this beta was not a common developed-market verdict on disinflation.

ECB communication limited the rally’s policy significance. The central bank had raised its deposit rate by 25 basis points to 2.25%, and Peter Kazimir argued that spreading price pressure would require further action. Euro-area inflation reached 3.2% in May, while the revised outlook kept core inflation above target through at least 2028. Markets still priced 1 additional increase during 2026 and a 70% chance of another in H1 of 2027. A peace agreement could lower energy prices quickly, but damaged production capacity and pipeline effects could keep broader inflation elevated.

The European debate was not uniformly hawkish. Some officials viewed the latest increase as sufficient pending more data, and sluggish activity constrained how far policy could move. That disagreement is itself relevant for US duration. A near-term ECB sequence raises the yield on competing high-grade assets, yet an eventual growth reversal can create demand for Bunds and Treasuries. The June 12 European rally reflected the 2nd channel; the US close retained more of the first.

UK data sharpened the same tension. Monthly GDP contracted 0.1% in April after 0.3% growth in March, the 1st decline since August 2025. Services fell 0.2%, production was flat and construction rose 0.1%. The 3 months through April still expanded 0.7%, slightly stronger than the preceding 3-month period. Gilt investors therefore faced a weak latest month without a clean collapse in momentum, allowing oil relief to support the front end but leaving the medium-term rate path dependent on inflation.

Household expectations kept the Bank of England constrained. Median 1-year inflation expectations rose to 4.0% from 3.2% in February, and the 5-year measure increased to 3.9% from 3.7%. A 53% majority expected interest rates to rise over the following year, up from 30%. Those readings challenge the idea that weaker monthly output alone can restore an easing cycle. They also explain why lower oil produced a large daily gilt rally without eliminating the risk of renewed policy restraint.

The Bundesbank's forecast quantified why Germany could support activity without eliminating the ECB's inflation problem. It expected GDP growth of 0.5% in 2026, 0.8% in 2027 and 1.4% in 2028 as public spending offset part of the war shock, while inflation reached 2.9% during the current year and 2.7% in 2027 before falling to 1.9% in 2028. Fiscal support improved the growth floor but could also slow disinflation, keeping German front-end policy risk distinct from the weak latest industrial data.

Poland moved in the opposite direction. MPC member Ireneusz Dabrowski said concern about another increase had receded across nearly the entire 10-member council after May inflation unexpectedly slowed to 3.1%, creating a possible route to a cut during 2026 from the 3.75% benchmark. The signal was conditional rather than a decision, but it sharpened the report's broader EM divergence: local inflation evidence, not the common oil shock alone, was determining whether central banks retained a tightening bias.

Weekend Australian evidence extended that divergence into developed markets. Economists expected the RBA to hold at 4.35% after 3 increases during 2026 as growth and employment softened and inflation momentum eased. Market-implied odds of another increase by December fell from fully priced to about 60%. Long-bond buyers targeted 10-year yields moving toward 4.5%, short-end investors anticipated eventual cuts, and defensive accounts preferred inflation-linked debt. Those positions agreed that the tightening cycle was near its limit but differed sharply on whether growth relief or persistent inflation would dominate.

Japan added a buyer-base problem at the long end. April data showed foreign investors sold more super-long JGBs than they purchased for the first time since 2024, as concerns about inflation, fiscal supply and a central bank perceived to be behind the curve outweighed multi-decade-high yields. Yet domestic demand was not absent. Iyogin began small super-long purchases in April, its first JGB investment in a decade, within a ¥1.7 trillion securities portfolio. Retreating foreign managers and selective regional-bank re-entry point to a higher, less stable clearing yield rather than a one-way loss of demand.

Weekend currency positioning added an asymmetric risk around the BOJ decision. Yen shorts reached their highest level in 9 years as the US-Japan rate gap sustained carry demand, even though a BOJ increase and foreign-exchange support were already substantially priced. The precedent from 2024 matters: a surprise hike and faster reduction in bond purchases forced a rapid unwind across currencies and equities. Crowded shorts could therefore amplify yen strength and global deleveraging if the BOJ exceeded expectations, while a fully anticipated move with cautious guidance could leave carry intact.

For Treasuries, these foreign developments operate through relative yield and hedging economics. European policy can keep front-end returns competitive, and volatile super-long JGBs can reduce the willingness of Japanese institutions to add overseas duration even when nominal US yields are high. Weak UK growth and selective domestic JGB demand provide offsets. The resulting competition helps explain why a large decline in crude was able to rally European bonds intraday but not carry the US curve through the New York close.

## EM Sovereigns, Dollar Liquidity, And Debt-Management Risk

Indonesia showed that local liquidity could remain impaired even when the global backdrop improved. Two bond funds delayed redemptions because selling government debt had become difficult after the asset rout and rupiah volatility. The KIM Fixed Income Fund Plus, reported at 5.7 trillion rupiah, fell 1.5% during the week through Thursday, while the 691.4 billion-rupiah sharia fund declined 0.7%. Bank Indonesia's retreat from bond purchases and off-cycle rate increase were intended to support the currency by allowing yields to rise, but they also tightened market liquidity. Redemption extensions moved the problem from price volatility into fund-liability management and showed why a currency-defense strategy can impair the domestic buyer base.

The common backdrop improved modestly for emerging-market debt. EMB rose 0.0935%, the dollar index softened and crude fell, reducing both US funding pressure and the prospective energy bill for oil importers. The small gain was far less emphatic than the move in equities or volatility, signaling that country-level fiscal and policy risks still limited the benefit. Bangladesh supplied a more direct energy-to-investment transmission. Gas shortages left almost $750 million of industrial projects stranded in the Cumilla economic zone, including steel, glass and aluminum capacity, while the average retail power tariff rose 17% and May inflation reached a 16-month high. The constraint reduced prospective productive capacity at the same time that households and companies faced higher energy costs. Unlike a temporary market-price shock, unavailable physical supply can weaken growth, tax receipts and external competitiveness even after global fuel prices ease.

India provided the clearest example because softer inflation and a potentially wider deficit pulled its sovereign curve in opposing directions.

Indian authorities were reported to be willing to let the fiscal deficit widen to as much as 4.8% of GDP from the 4.3% target if the global environment required it. The country imports more than 80% of its crude, and higher fuel and fertilizer subsidies have opened pressure on the budget. India’s 10-year yield briefly reached 6.91% before returning to 6.88%. 1 estimate placed possible additional bill borrowing at 350 billion rupees, making the debt-management channel a concrete consequence rather than an accounting revision alone.

Current inflation data offered an offset. May CPI rose 3.93% from a year earlier, below the 4.02% consensus and just under the Reserve Bank of India’s 4% target. The 10-year yield retained gains at 6.89% after the release. Food inflation accelerated to 4.78% from 4.20%, and the RBI had already lifted its fiscal-year inflation projection to 5.1% from 4.6%. The sovereign benefited from a softer headline print, but food, currency and subsidy exposure kept fiscal credibility and the borrowing response central to the curve.

Brazil faced the opposite inflation surprise. Consumer prices rose 0.58% in May, above the 0.53% median estimate, and annual inflation reached 4.72%, beyond the 4.5% upper edge of the target range. Food and beverage prices increased 1.33%, and underlying pressure extended beyond components most directly tied to the war. With the Selic rate already at 14.5%, the release narrowed the room for further easing and preserved high local carry at the cost of tighter domestic financing conditions.

Policy divergence spread across the emerging complex. Indonesia had used an off-cycle increase to stabilize its currency and reverse a selloff, whereas softer inflation opened debate about easing in Poland and Hungary. Romania’s 3-year-high inflation argued for a hold, and Czech officials kept a possible increase in view. Oil-importing Asian economies remained more exposed to renewed crude strength than high-carry markets backed by credible frameworks. A slightly softer dollar could ease the common constraint without resolving those differences in inflation dynamics or central-bank credibility.

Venezuela's weekend adviser contest created a concrete fee and governance delta in its prospective restructuring. Lazard offered to oversee the estimated $150 billion to $200 billion workout for $25 million, far below the at-least $150 million arrangement Centerview had discussed, including a 0.1% uncapped success fee and $750,000 monthly retainer. No adviser replacement or creditor terms had been finalized. The competing bids nevertheless showed that process costs were contestable and that mandate governance could materially affect value before bond, loan, arbitration and other claims were reconciled.

Subsovereign access remained narrower than national policy flexibility. Jakarta continued to examine Indonesia’s first municipal bond after central-government transfers were cut by about 15 trillion rupiah, roughly 16% of its initial budget. Finance Ministry approval for the bond and a proposed wealth fund was still outstanding. The plan could diversify infrastructure funding, but its regulatory dependence and reduced transfers show why local credit creation cannot be treated as sovereign market access. Across EM, lower oil helped the daily backdrop; refinancing structure, reserve use and the credibility of fiscal adjustment still determined the usable relief.

## Cross asset

Equities reinforced the interpretation that Treasuries lost a haven bid rather than responding to weaker growth. The S&P 500 rose 0.5026%, the Nasdaq 100 gained 0.6445%, and the semiconductor index advanced 1.5187%. Technology leadership was consistent with confidence in nominal activity and continued AI capital spending. That mix supports higher real discount rates at the front and belly even when cheaper energy improves the inflation outlook.

Volatility and the dollar pointed in the same risk-on direction. The VIX fell 9.0535% to 17.68, and the dollar index slipped 0.1102% to 99.75. Lower volatility reduced the demand for defensive duration, while the softer dollar eased the external financing backdrop for emerging borrowers. The combination did not resemble a global dollar shortage or generalized deleveraging, helping explain the stability of high-yield fund prices.

Energy created the session’s most important contradiction. WTI fell 3.2265% to $84.88 and Brent declined 3.3746% to $87.33 as negotiations raised hopes of reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Yet Treasury breakevens and nominal yields ended higher. The disconnect indicates that the market had already captured much of the immediate de-escalation benefit on June 11 and was turning toward lagged inflation, resilient activity and the Fed’s reaction function. Cheaper crude improved the distribution of outcomes without dictating the closing direction of rates.

Gold did not fully endorse the benign interpretation. Futures rose 3.0487% to $4,215 even as equities advanced, oil fell and volatility declined. The move left demand for inflation or geopolitical protection active despite optimism around negotiations. It also prevented the cross-asset picture from becoming a simple unwind of war risk. Gold’s gain sat alongside higher breakevens as a reminder that an agreement had not yet restored damaged supply capacity or eliminated uncertainty over implementation.

The record SpaceX flotation illustrated the scale of risk appetite. Shares opened at $150 against a $135 offer price, traded as high as $163 and finished their debut 19% higher after a $75 billion offering. Absorbing that volume alongside rising broad equity indexes showed deep demand for growth exposure. It also reinforced the capital-intensity channel behind elevated real rates: AI and infrastructure spending continued to compete for savings even as geopolitical relief reduced the immediate inflation premium.

## Forward Market Significance

US activity, trade-price and consumption data from June 15 through June 17 culminate in the Federal Open Market Committee decision at 14:00 ET on June 17 and Chair Kevin Warsh’s first post-meeting press conference at 14:30. The observable trigger is whether industrial production and retail sales remain resilient as import prices cool, followed by a dot plot and statement that retain or remove an explicit tightening bias. Firm demand, broad trade-price gains or projections pointing to an increase would pressure 2- and 5-year yields and confirm June 12’s renewed policy premium. Softer activity, receding price breadth and neutral guidance would challenge the earlier-hike interpretation and restore the lower-real-yield channel opened on June 11.

After the June 12 cutoff, Pakistan’s prime minister said the US and Iran had agreed to an immediate cessation of military operations, removal of the US naval blockade and a formal signing in Switzerland on June 19. Implementation now tests whether Friday’s oil decline becomes a durable disinflation impulse. Observable triggers are sustained passage through the Strait of Hormuz, no renewed hostilities, lower crude and a retreat in household or market inflation expectations. Delivery would confirm that energy relief can eventually pull breakevens and global front ends lower; slippage before the signing, renewed blockade risk or persistent core pressure would challenge that view and reopen the inflation premium despite cheaper spot oil.

The June 15-18 Treasury calendar tests whether balance-sheet capacity remains orderly as policy uncertainty rises. The sequence begins with $89 billion of 13-week and $77 billion of 26-week bills on June 15, followed by a $65 billion 6-week bill and $13 billion 20-year reopening on June 16, then a $24 billion 5-year TIPS reopening on June 18; the June 19 fixed-income holiday shortens the reaction window. Observable triggers are bill demand, funding rates, the 20-year stop against its when-issued level, bidder allocation and real-yield demand. Strong end-user absorption with stable cash rates would resolve near-term supply concern and confirm a macro-led selloff. Heavy dealer awards, a tail or funding strain would reopen fiscal supply as an independent source of term-premium pressure.

overall_summary.headline: Treasury rally fades as renewed Fed restraint outweighs cheaper oil
overall_summary.session_narrative: Treasuries initially followed European bonds higher as progress toward a US-Iran agreement pushed crude lower. The move reversed in New York, leaving the curve modestly cheaper and flatter as firmer sentiment and still-elevated inflation expectations rebuilt Fed restraint in the front end. Stable credit and an orderly long bond limited the signal: this was policy and haven-demand repricing, not a broad financing or fiscal shock.
overall_summary.summary: The curve ended modestly cheaper, led by the policy-sensitive front end, even as crude fell again. Better sentiment, still-high inflation expectations and resilient risk appetite rebuilt near-term Fed premium, while stable credit and an orderly long end argued against a broader financing or fiscal shock.
